text:
maria (support): FYI customer reported a burst of 502s when sending batched embeddings (1000 items) to the hosted API around 08:12 UTC. They provided a sample request id: req_8f3b2c. Error is a 502 with body 'upstream error: connection reset by peer'. Impacting 3 customers.
jamal (eng-sre): Can you paste the request headers + trace id? Also any correlation with deploys?
maria (support): trace_id=trace-6b9a, headers they sent: `Content-Type: application/json`, `Connection: keep-alive`, payload ~18MB. No deploys in the last hour per deploy-bot. They said retries make it worse.
jamal (eng-sre): grabbing logs now. quick grep shows a flurry of `upstream reset` from midproxy pool and a bunch of `HTTP/2 RST_STREAM` on the frontdoor. Looks like midproxy backends were ejected by Envoy outlier detector: `ejection_type: consecutive_5xx`, hosts ejected ~30s each.
alex (eng-runtime): We recently raised `max_concurrent_streams` on the midproxy-to-backend connection to 1000 for smaller latencies, but the midproxy threads hit CPU saturation during big batches. When CPU is high the accept/dispatch stalls and Envoy sees short-lived 5xx and ejects hosts.
sasha (eng-infra): Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) temporarily reduce `max_concurrent_streams` to 200, 2) increase midproxy pool size by +2 instances, 3) bump Envoy outlier ejection threshold (consecutive_5xx -> 6) so we don't evict on transient spike. Which is lowest-risk to roll?
jamal (eng-sre): Plan: roll a config patch to increase pool size (low-risk), add an emergency flag to disable outlier ejection for 2 minutes (needs review), and prepare rollback for the `max_concurrent_streams` change. I'll also pin the affected customers to a lower concurrency quota for embeddings.
maria (support): Provided reproducer to eng: customer curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large","inputs":[...1000 items...]}'
```
They see 50% request success, 50% 502, mostly during the first minute of a burst.
alex (eng-runtime): I ran a small internal repro with 500 concurrent items and saw the midproxy CPU spike + `accept()` latency grow to 300ms. Patch suggestion: add simple backpressure at midproxy accept loop (reject above 250 concurrent streams) + rate-limit per connection for batch endpoints. I'll prepare a PR.
jamal (eng-sre): For immediate support triage: can support lower the customer's concurrency to 10 requests/min and ask them to retry staggered? That should stop the ejection loop until infra patch lands.
maria (support): Done — told customer to set concurrency throttle and stagger; they confirmed lower error rate. Also shared temporary workaround: use smaller batch sizes (<200) or switch to the embeddings streaming endpoint. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Alert posted to #incidents: `midproxy_ejection_spike - 502s` (severity: medium).
jamal (eng-sre): Next steps: 1) schedule canary for midproxy pool + outlier config in 30m, 2) merge runtime PR for accept-loop backpressure (post-canary), 3) longer-term: autoscale midproxy by in-flight streams rather than CPU. I'll own the roll and post updates.
maria (support): thanks — keeping customer informed. Will reopen if errors return after canary.
jamal (eng-sre): FYI logs/commands for trace hunting: `rg trace-6b9a /var/log/proxy/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'` and HTTP dump: `sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 -w /tmp/midproxy.pcap port 443 and host <customer-ip>` — shared with eng on secure channel.
alex (eng-runtime): noted. PR link (will post once CI is green) and I'll include a small loadtest plan to validate no regressions.
end of thread
